blocks.text: We have learnt that a charge experiences an electrostatic force in the presence of other charges. Let us consider a positively charged object O. If we place a small charge +q at point A, it will experience an electrostatic force F due to the charged body O. Thus, an electric field is said to exist at point A. Coulomb's law suggests that the field gets stronger as the point A gets closer to O as represented in Fig. 9.3. The strength of the field at a position is known as its intensity at that point.

blocks.alt: A circle O filled with + signs (a positively charged body). A dashed line leads from O to point A, where a small orange charge +q sits; a red arrow F continues from A directly away from O.
blocks.caption: Figure 9.3 (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 9.3).

blocks.title: Electric intensity
blocks.text: The electric intensity of the field or simply electric field at any point is defined as the force experienced by a unit positive charge placed at that point.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: Electric intensity is the force per unit positive charge (E = F/q), not a force; its unit is N C⁻¹. It is a vector because force is a vector and charge q is a scalar.

blocks.text: Both references should be to Eq. 9.8 (E = F/q), not Eq. 9.5, which is Coulomb's force in vector form.

blocks.title: Example 9.2
blocks.problem: Two positive point charges q₁ = 16.0 μC and q₂ = 4.0 μC are separated by a distance of 3.0 m, as shown in Fig. 9.4. Find the spot on the line joining the two charges where electric field is zero.
steps: Between the two charges, the fields contributed by them have opposite directions, and electric field would be zero at a point P, where the magnitude of E₁ equals to E₂. In Fig. 9.4, let the distance of P from q₂ be d. At P, E₁ = E₂ which implies that:
or d² + 2d − 3 = 0, which gives d = +1 m, −3 m

There are two values of d, the negative value corresponds to a location off to the right of both the charges where magnitudes of E₁ and E₂ are equal but directions are same. In this case E₁ and E₂ do not cancel at this spot. The positive value corresponds to the location shown in the figure and is the zero filed location,

blocks.title: Example 9.3
blocks.problem: A proton experiences an electrostatic force equal to its weight at a particular point in an electric field. What is the field intensity at that point? Mass of proton = 1.67 × 10⁻²⁷ kg and charge, e = 1.6 × 10⁻¹⁹ C
